en_zh_sota.name: Qwen3-Embedding (0.6B / 4B / 8B)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 8B: MTEB-Multilingual 70.58 (beat Gemini-Embedding); 0.6B: 64.34 with 600M params; 100+ languages, 32k context, Matryoshka dims, Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The bar for open multilingual embedders; the 0.6B is the exact size class a solo engineer can fine-tune on RTX 2070/modest cloud — natural base for a Kazakh embedder

en_zh_sota.name: Qwen3-Reranker (0.6B / 4B / 8B)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 4B: MTEB-R 69.76; 8B: CMTEB-R 77.45, MTEB-Code 81.22; 0.6B already beats prior SOTA rerankers; Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The reranker bar and the ideal distillation teacher (score kk query-passage pairs with 8B, distill into a small cross-encoder)

en_zh_sota.name: BGE-M3 (BAAI)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 567M params, dense + sparse + multi-vector (ColBERT) in one model, 8192 ctx, 100+ languages incl. kk, MIT license, 32M monthly HF downloads
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Defines the 'hybrid retrieval in one checkpoint' standard; de-facto what Kazakh RAG builders use today; the model to beat on kk

en_zh_sota.name: multilingual-e5 family (small/base/large, large-instruct)
en_zh_sota.numbers: small 118M / base 278M / large 560M, 94 languages, MIT; mE5-large scores MRR 0.909 on KazQAD-hard-negatives — currently the de-facto best Kazakh retriever, beating all existing Kazakh fine-tunes
en_zh_sota.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05672 ; kazembed-v5 model card benchmark table https://huggingface.co/Nurlykhan/kazembed-v5
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The workhorse baseline; both existing Kazakh community embedders are mE5-base fine-tunes; mE5-large is the concrete number the author's embedding-goal must beat

en_zh_sota.name: EmbeddingGemma-300m (Google)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 308M params, MTEB-Multilingual-v2 61.15 — best under 500M; 100+ languages, 2k ctx, QAT int4 on-device, Gemma license; 1.5M monthly downloads
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Proof that a ~300M model can be near-SOTA multilingual — the efficiency template for a Kazakh-first small embedder matching the author's SLM philosophy

en_zh_sota.name: jina-embeddings-v3
en_zh_sota.numbers: 570M, 89 languages, task-specific LoRA adapters, 8192 ctx, MRL; license CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Shows the task-LoRA-adapter recipe; its non-commercial license illustrates the market opening for a permissively-licensed regional embedder

en_zh_sota.name: bge-reranker-v2-m3
en_zh_sota.numbers: 568M multilingual cross-encoder on BGE-M3 backbone, Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The standard open multilingual reranker and best fine-tuning base for a first Kazakh reranker (kk is in its pretraining coverage)

en_zh_sota.name: gte-multilingual-base (Alibaba)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 305M, 70+ languages incl. kk, 8192 ctx, elastic dims, Apache-2.0, 1.24M monthly downloads
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Efficient long-context multilingual baseline that must appear in any kk leaderboard

en_zh_sota.name: MTEB / MMTEB + C-MTEB ecosystem
en_zh_sota.numbers: MMTEB: 500+ tasks, 250+ languages, community-PR model (ICLR 2025); C-MTEB: 35 Chinese datasets over 6 task types; Kazakh coverage today = only translated peripheral tasks (BelebeleRetrieval, Flores/NTREX bitext mining, SIB-200) — zero native kk retrieval/STS/reranking tasks (verified by code search of embeddings-benchmark/mteb, July 2026)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The eval infrastructure every language community copies (PL-MTEB, FaMTEB, VN-MTEB, ruMTEB, AfriMTEB); the exact playbook for kk-MTEB — and PRs get merged

en_zh_sota.name: Gemini Embedding (API ceiling)
en_zh_sota.numbers: MTEB-Multilingual 68.32, Borda #1 at launch (Mar 2025); by 2026 open models (Qwen3-8B 70.58, NVIDIA Llama-Embed-Nemotron-8B per 2026 leaderboards — secondary source, uncertain) match/surpass it
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The proprietary ceiling; shows open-weight models now win multilingual — a regional player can realistically top a language-specific board

gaps.gap: No Kazakh embedding benchmark exists (no kk-MTEB; KazQAD never integrated into MTEB; zero native kk retrieval/STS/rerank tasks in the standard suite)
gaps.why: Nobody can measure 'best Kazakh embedder' — the two existing community fine-tunes use incompatible self-made evals; every language community that built its MTEB subset (PL, FA, VN, RU, AfriMTEB) instantly became the citation anchor. This blocks the author's embedding-goal from being provable

gaps.gap: No human-verified Kazakh STS dataset — the only STS resource is a machine-translated STS-B with 5 downloads and no quality check
gaps.why: STS is the canonical embedding eval axis; without it, semantic-similarity quality for kk is literally unmeasurable, and agglutinative morphology + code-switching make MT-only STS untrustworthy

gaps.gap: No Kazakh reranker exists at all (zero cross-encoders, zero rerank training data)
gaps.why: Reranking gives the largest quality-per-dollar jump in RAG; every kk RAG system today either skips reranking or uses multilingual rerankers never tested on Kazakh

gaps.gap: No Kazakh fine-tune beats off-the-shelf mE5-large/BGE-M3 — the 'best Kazakh embedding model' title is factually unclaimed
gaps.why: Existing fine-tunes are base-size and lose to large multilingual models on their own benchmarks (0.835 vs 0.909 MRR); a properly-trained model with mined pairs + hard negatives would take the crown with modest compute

gaps.gap: No published contrastive training corpus for kk (no msmarco-kk, no mined triplets, no hard-negative sets) despite abundant feedstock (KazParC 372k, OPUS millions of pairs, SNLI-kk 570k, 800k wiki passages)
gaps.why: Training data is the actual bottleneck; the feedstock exists but nobody has done the mining/filtering work, so every fine-tune starts from scratch on tiny KazQAD

gaps.gap: No morphology-aware lexical baseline packaged for modern stacks — Kazakh BM25 with proper stemming/lemmatization is not available in bm25s/Elastic 8/Qdrant hybrid pipelines
gaps.why: Agglutinative morphology (rich suffixation) makes raw-token BM25 much weaker than it should be; a solid lexical baseline is required for honest hybrid-vs-dense comparisons in any benchmark paper

gaps.gap: Key eval/training datasets (KazQAD, KazParC, KazSANDRA) are gated on HF behind login walls
gaps.why: Gating breaks `mteb run` reproducibility and CI evals; GitHub copies are open, so re-hosting with permission is straightforward but nobody has done it

gaps.gap: kk-ru code-switched retrieval is completely untested — no eval measures mixed-script/mixed-language queries against kk documents
gaps.why: Real Kazakhstani users mix Kazakh and Russian in queries constantly; production retrieval quality is unknown and likely poor, and no benchmark captures it

tasks.task: kk-MTEB v0: write MTEB task classes for KazQADRetrieval (from the open GitHub copy of issai/kazqad-retrieval), KazSANDRAClassification, and KazakhSTSb (sultanbi/stsb-kazakh test split, flagged as MT), PR them to embeddings-benchmark/mteb, then run ~15 models (mE5 small/base/large, BGE-M3, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, EmbeddingGemma-300m, gte-multilingual-base, LaBSE, arctic-embed-m/l-v2, jina-v3, nomic-v2-moe, kazembed-v5, kazakh-e5-rag-embedding) and publish the first Kazakh embedding leaderboard as an HF Space
tasks.deliverable: Merged MTEB PR + public kk leaderboard Space + results table (CSV on HF)
tasks.data_needed: KazQAD from github.com/IS2AI/KazQAD (CC BY-SA, needs re-hosting as ungated HF dataset with qrels config); KazSANDRA from github.com/IS2AI/KazSAnDRA; sultanbi/stsb-kazakh

tasks.task: KazSTS-human: human-verify the 1,379-pair stsb-kazakh test split — post-edit MT with Tilmash/NLLB cross-checks, re-score similarity 0-5 with 2 native annotators in Label Studio, report inter-annotator agreement; this becomes the canonical kk STS test set
tasks.deliverable: ~1.4k human-verified STS pairs on HF (CC BY 4.0) + Spearman baseline table for 15 embedders + MTEB task PR
tasks.data_needed: sultanbi/stsb-kazakh test split; 2 native-speaker annotators (~30-40 hours total annotation)

tasks.task: Contrastive pair factory: mine kk-ru/kk-en positives from KazParC (371,902 CC BY 4.0 pairs) + OPUS (CCMatrix/NLLB/WikiMatrix kk-ru, kk-en), filter with LaBSE cosine >= 0.8 margin criterion, add in-language kk-kk positives via round-trip translation (Tilmash) and adjacent-sentence pairs from kk Wikipedia/CulturaX
tasks.deliverable: kk-contrastive-1M dataset on HF (query/positive pairs, provenance-tagged, Apache-2.0)
tasks.data_needed: KazParC (GitHub), OPUS downloads, LaBSE for filtering (runs on RTX 2070), issai/tilmash for round-trip

tasks.task: Hard-negative mining pipeline: for each KazQAD question and translated NQ-kk training query, retrieve top-100 from the 800k kk-Wikipedia passage corpus with BM25 (Kazakh stemmer) + mE5-large, remove false negatives with an LLM judge (Qwen3-32B or KazLLM-8B via cheap API/local), emit msmarco-style (query, positive, hard-negative) triplets
tasks.deliverable: kk-triplets dataset (100-500k triplets) on HF — the first reusable kk contrastive training set with hard negatives
tasks.data_needed: KazQAD corpus + questions (GitHub), output of the pair factory, one judge LLM (local Qwen3 quantized or ~$50 API budget)
tasks.depends_on: Contrastive pair factory (shares infrastructure, can run in parallel)

tasks.task: Train the flagship Kazakh embedder: fine-tune Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (primary; Apache-2.0, MRL, 32k ctx) and mE5-large (fallback) with CachedMultipleNegativesRankingLoss (GradCache for large effective batch on RTX 2070 / one rented A100-day) on kk-contrastive-1M + kk-triplets + cleaned SNLI-kk; success criterion: beat mE5-large's MRR 0.909 on KazQAD and rank #1 on kk-MTEB
tasks.deliverable: The best Kazakh embedding model on HF (Apache-2.0) + kk-MTEB #1 entry + training recipe repo
tasks.data_needed: Outputs of tasks 3, 4, 9; kk-MTEB (task 1) as the referee
tasks.depends_on: kk-MTEB v0, contrastive pair factory, hard-negative mining

tasks.task: First Kazakh reranker via distillation: score 100-300k kk (query, passage) pairs from the triplet set with Qwen3-Reranker-4B/8B as teacher, distill into bge-reranker-v2-m3 (568M) with MSE/margin loss; evaluate NDCG@10 uplift over BM25 top-100 and dense top-100 on KazQAD
tasks.deliverable: kk-reranker on HF (Apache-2.0) — the first Kazakh reranker in existence + eval table
tasks.data_needed: kk-triplets (task 4); teacher inference ~1 GPU-day (rentable, ~$30)

tasks.task: Morphology-aware lexical baseline package: wrap Apertium-kaz lemmatization (or port the Kazakh-Stemmer-Elasticsearch-Plugin rules to Python) as a bm25s-compatible tokenizer/analyzer; benchmark stemmed-BM25 vs raw-BM25 vs dense vs hybrid RRF on KazQAD; publish as pip-installable package
tasks.deliverable: kk-bm25 package on PyPI + benchmark numbers (the lexical baseline every future kk IR paper will cite)
tasks.data_needed: Apertium-kaz (GitHub, GPL — or reimplement stemmer rules), KazQAD, bm25s

tasks.task: kk-ru code-switch retrieval eval: build 300-500 mixed-language/mixed-script queries by (a) translating KazQAD dev queries to Russian, (b) creating realistic kk-ru blended variants (LLM-generated, human-spot-checked), then measure every leaderboard embedder's degradation retrieving kk passages from ru and mixed queries
tasks.deliverable: kk-ru-codeswitch eval set on HF + degradation table (a first-of-kind finding for the atlas and a differentiator for the flagship embedder's training data)
tasks.data_needed: KazQAD dev queries, Tilmash/NLLB for translation, LLM for blending, ~10h native review

tasks.task: Clean SNLI-kk into AllNLI-kk training triplets: filter sultanbi/snli-kazakh (~570k MT pairs) with LaBSE en-kk agreement scoring + length-ratio heuristics, drop bottom ~30%, format as (anchor, entailment, contradiction) triplets for SBERT-style training
tasks.deliverable: allnli-kk-clean dataset on HF (~300-400k triplets, CC BY-SA 4.0)
tasks.data_needed: sultanbi/snli-kazakh, LaBSE (local GPU is enough)

tasks.task: On-device/product variant: apply Matryoshka truncation (768->512/256/128/64) plus int8 ONNX export to the flagship embedder; ship a demo — semantic search over all of Kazakh Wikipedia running in-browser or on a $5 VPS with Qdrant
tasks.deliverable: Quantized model + live demo Space + blog post ('semantic search for Kazakh on a laptop') — the product-marketing artifact for the embedding goal
tasks.data_needed: Flagship embedder (task 5), kk Wikipedia dump (wikimedia/wikipedia 20xx.kk)

tasks.task: Tokenizer-fertility vs retrieval-quality study: measure each embedder's tokenizer fertility on kk (multilingual models: 4.7-4.9 tokens/word) against its kk-MTEB scores; replicate the Turkish 'cross-lingual tokenizer surgery + offline distillation' recipe (arXiv 2605.29992) on mE5-base with the Til-Tokenizer-128k or QymyzLM tokenizer
tasks.deliverable: Analysis notebook + short arXiv note + (if surgery works) a fertility-fixed kk embedder variant; shared tokenizer findings flow directly into QymyzLM
tasks.data_needed: kk-MTEB results (task 1), TilQazyna/Til-Tokenizer-128k, mE5-base, kk corpus sample for fertility measurement

tasks.task: kk-MTEB paper: after tasks 1, 2, 8 land, write the benchmark paper — 'kk-MTEB: a Kazakh text embedding benchmark and the first systematic evaluation of N embedders for Kazakh' (LREC/COLING or arXiv), following the PL-MTEB/FaMTEB template; include the code-switch and fertility findings as novel analyses
tasks.deliverable: arXiv paper + citeable leaderboard — the anchor citation for the atlas survey and the author's name on the measurement standard
tasks.data_needed: All eval results from tasks 1, 2, 8, 11

sectors.flagship_opportunity: Own the measurement layer, then top it: ship kk-MTEB (first Kazakh embedding benchmark — merged into upstream MTEB, with a human-verified KazSTS and the first kk leaderboard) and simultaneously train the embedder that ranks #1 on it by beating off-the-shelf mE5-large (MRR 0.909 on KazQAD), which no Kazakh model has ever done. Whoever defines the benchmark defines 'best Kazakh embedding model' — and today that seat, the training data (no mined triplets exist), the reranker (zero exist), and the STS dataset (one unverified MT file with 5 downloads) are all completely unclaimed, while the feedstock (KazQAD, KazParC, OPUS, 800k wiki passages) sits ready. Total cost: roughly one month of solo work plus under $100 of cloud compute.

en_zh_sota.name: Qwen3-TTS (Alibaba)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 0.6B and 1.7B variants (12Hz codec); Apache-2.0; trained on ~5M hours; 10 languages incl. Russian (no Kazakh); 3-second zero-shot voice cloning; reported ~97ms streaming latency; released Jan 2026
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Best finetune base for Kazakh today: open license, small size (0.6B mirrors the QymyzLM-vs-Qwen3-0.6B narrative), built-in cloning and streaming, already knows Russian (half of the kk-ru code-switch problem)

en_zh_sota.name: CosyVoice 3 (FunAudioLLM)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1.5B LM + 300M flow-matching (up from 0.5B+100M in v2); 1M hours training; 9 languages incl. Russian + 18 Chinese dialects; Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 open on HF; CosyVoice2-0.5B ~150ms streaming latency, Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The 'in-the-wild' zero-shot bar: content consistency + speaker similarity + prosody at scale; the v2 0.5B is the alternative Kazakh finetune base with a proven low-resource-language finetune community

en_zh_sota.name: F5-TTS
en_zh_sota.numbers: ~336M DiT flow-matching; zero-shot cloning with high speaker similarity; code MIT, released weights CC-BY-NC (Emilia data); full finetune supported, widely replicated for new languages
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The proven 'add a new language with ~100h' recipe — dozens of community language finetunes; the fallback base if codec-LLM routes disappoint

en_zh_sota.name: Kokoro-82M
en_zh_sota.numbers: 82M params; Apache-2.0; <0.3s synthesis on CPU-class hardware; 8 languages; no voice cloning
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The on-device/throughput bar — what a Kazakh screen-reader / edge voice should aspire to in size and speed

en_zh_sota.name: Fish Audio OpenAudio S1/S2
en_zh_sota.numbers: S1-mini 0.5B (CC-BY-NC-SA); S2 claims 80+ languages, ~100ms time-to-first-audio on hosted SGLang engine; only EN/JA/ZH at top quality
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The commercial-grade streaming + multilingual-cloning bar; shows 'claims 80 languages' does not equal quality — exactly the trap a Kazakh benchmark must expose

en_zh_sota.name: IndexTTS-2 (bilibili)
en_zh_sota.numbers: Autoregressive zero-shot TTS with explicit duration control and emotion fidelity; beats prior zero-shot systems on WER/speaker-sim/emotion per authors; weights under bilibili-indextts license (not Apache)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The emotion + duration control bar; already has one (flawed, single-speaker) Kazakh finetune proving the route is trainable

en_zh_sota.name: ElevenLabs Eleven v3
en_zh_sota.numbers: Proprietary API; 74 languages INCLUDING Kazakh (kaz); high emotional range; kk STT at 5-10% WER tier
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The absolute quality bar — and it already ships Kazakh, so any open Kazakh model must benchmark against it; its kk quality is unverified publicly (no MOS/CER data — exactly what KazTTS-Bench should measure)

en_zh_sota.name: Meta MMS-TTS
en_zh_sota.numbers: Per-language VITS checkpoints for 1100+ languages; mms-tts-kaz is the most-downloaded kk TTS (~1.2k downloads); CC-BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The coverage floor Kazakh currently sits on: single robotic voice, non-commercial license — beating it decisively is the minimum viable contribution

en_zh_sota.name: Microsoft VibeVoice-1.5B
en_zh_sota.numbers: Up to 90 minutes of multi-speaker long-form speech, 4 speakers; EN/ZH only
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The long-form/audiobook-podcast bar — relevant because audiobooks are a concrete Kazakh product niche (Kazakh literature digitization) with zero current tooling

kazakh_existing.status: Usable but weak: single-voice VITS, CC-BY-NC 4.0 (blocks commercial use), most-downloaded kk TTS (~1,240 downloads) purely by default — the bar to beat publicly

kazakh_existing.name: Common Voice Kazakh
kazakh_existing.status: Nearly empty: v24.0 has 3.76h recorded / 2.39h validated from 193 speakers, 6,470 sentences in the text bank. Community pipeline effectively dead

kazakh_existing.name: Commercial layer: Yandex SpeechKit, Azure, ElevenLabs, Nanosemantics/3iTech
kazakh_existing.status: Usable but paid/closed: Yandex SpeechKit has 4 kk voices (Madi, Amira, Zhanar, Saule) + improved kk normalizer + Karaganda data center; Azure has kk-KZ AigulNeural/DauletNeural; ElevenLabs v3 covers Kazakh; Nanosemantics NLab and 3iTech sell kk TTS. ISSAI's Soyle app ships kk TTS as a product. No open weights from any of them

kazakh_existing.name: RHVoice / accessibility stack
kazakh_existing.status: GAP EVIDENCE: RHVoice supports Kyrgyz, Tatar, Turkmen, Uzbek — but NOT Kazakh (as of June 2025 language list). No Piper kk voice either. Screen-reader users have only eSpeak-NG-grade or paid options

gaps.gap: No Kazakh TTS benchmark, leaderboard, or eval protocol exists; all four 2026 community finetunes ship with zero quality metrics (no MOS, no CER, no speaker-sim)
gaps.why: Nobody — including the model authors — can say which kk TTS is best, whether ElevenLabs' kk is actually good, or whether a new finetune improved anything. Every downstream task needs this measuring stick first. It is also the cheapest field-defining artifact available (pure inference + scoring on an RTX 2070)

gaps.gap: No open zero-shot voice cloning that generalizes for Kazakh — and no multi-speaker TTS-grade corpus to train one (KazakhTTS2 has only 5 speakers; IndexTTS2-Kazakh's card admits cloning collapses to the training speaker)
gaps.why: Cloning is the defining capability of the 2025-26 TTS generation (CosyVoice3/Qwen3-TTS do it from 3s). The blocker is data shape, not architecture: KSC2's 1.2k ASR hours (MIT) have the speakers but need quality filtering to become TTS-grade

gaps.gap: Open Kazakh TTS architecture is 3-4 years behind SOTA: official ISSAI models are Tacotron2+WaveGAN (2021), best emotional model is GradTTS at MOS 3.5; the only modern-arch models are unevaluated hobbyist finetunes; only high-quality kk TTS is closed/paid (Yandex/Azure/ElevenLabs)
gaps.why: 271h CC-BY data + Apache-2.0 0.6B bases (Qwen3-TTS) exist — the ingredients for a modern open model are all on the table, unassembled. Sovereignty angle: Kazakh voice tech currently rents from Moscow, Redmond, and NYC

gaps.gap: No code-switch kk-ru synthesis support or evaluation anywhere — no CS-TTS dataset, no CS eval set; only Yandex claims mixed kk-ru handling (in ASR, closed)
gaps.why: Real Kazakhstani text is saturated with Russian words, names, and intra-word switches (Kazakh stems + Russian suffixes); a kk-only TTS mangles half of realistic input. KazakhTTS2 papers acknowledge the problem but no artifact addresses it

gaps.gap: No open Kazakh text-normalization frontend (numbers→words with case agreement, dates, ₸, abbreviations) and zero Latin-script support despite the official 2023-2031 transition
gaps.why: Agglutinative morphology makes number expansion non-trivial (case endings attach to the number word); every existing model chokes on '2026 жылдың 15 қаңтарында' raw. Latin 2021-alphabet input is supported by no TTS on earth — a cheap 'first' as government/media Latin usage grows

gaps.gap: No lightweight on-device / accessibility voice: RHVoice has no Kazakh, no Piper kk voice exists, mms-tts-kaz is CC-BY-NC and single-voice
gaps.why: Blind kk-speaking screen-reader users and offline/edge products (Home Assistant, e-readers, kiosks) have no free option; a Kokoro/Piper-class kk voice is trainable on one RTX 2070 from KazakhTTS2

gaps.gap: Community speech data pipeline is dead: Common Voice kk has 2.39 validated hours (193 speakers) vs. hundreds of hours for peer languages
gaps.why: Institutional data (ISSAI) papered over this, but CC0 community data is what feeds cloning diversity, dialect coverage, and future models nobody has to license

tasks.task: KazTTS-Bench: first public Kazakh TTS benchmark + leaderboard. Build 500-sentence eval set across 5 domains (held-out KazakhTTS2 news, Wikipedia, conversational, numeric/date-heavy, kk-ru code-switched). Score every system found in this survey (mms-tts-kaz, ISSAI ESPnet, Spark-TTS-Kazakh, VoxCPM-KazakhTTS-Lora, IndexTTS2-Kazakh, qwen3-tts-kazakh-emotional, Azure kk-KZ, Yandex SpeechKit, ElevenLabs v3) on ASR-CER (Whisper-large-v3 cross-checked with ISSAI ASR), UTMOS-style naturalness proxy, and RTF/latency
tasks.deliverable: HF dataset (eval set) + HF Space leaderboard + scoring scripts on GitHub; the survey's measured table
tasks.data_needed: 500 curated sentences (existing public text + own writing); API credits ~$20 for commercial systems

tasks.task: QymyzVoice-0.6B: finetune Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base (Apache-2.0) on KazakhTTS2 (271h, CC BY 4.0) + KazEmoTTS (74.85h, CC BY 4.0). Pipeline: resample/segment to Qwen3-TTS 12Hz codec format, LoRA pilot on RTX 2070 to validate data pipeline, then full finetune on a rented A100 (~$150-300). Mirrors the QymyzLM-vs-Qwen3-0.6B story in speech
tasks.deliverable: Apache-2.0 model on HF that tops the KazTTS-Bench open track; demo Space
tasks.data_needed: KazakhTTS2 + KazEmoTTS (both open, downloadable today); ~$300 cloud GPU

tasks.task: KazClone-Eval: zero-shot voice-cloning evaluation protocol for Kazakh. 20 held-out KSC2 speakers x 3s/10s reference prompts; metrics: ECAPA-TDNN cosine speaker similarity + ASR-CER + naturalness. Run on all cloning-claiming systems (Spark-TTS-Kazakh, VoxCPM-KazakhTTS-Lora, IndexTTS2-Kazakh) plus cross-lingual zero-shot from Qwen3-TTS/CosyVoice3 base models (measures how far ru-trained bases get on kk with no finetune — a publishable negative/positive result either way)
tasks.deliverable: Cloning leaderboard section of KazTTS-Bench + short report; exposes which 'supports cloning' claims are real
tasks.data_needed: KSC2 speaker-labeled subset (MIT, on HF)

tasks.task: qazaq-tts-norm: open Kazakh text-normalization frontend. Number-to-word with agglutinative case agreement (15-інде → он бесінде), dates, ₸/currency, abbreviations, phone numbers, ru-loanword detection, and a 2021-official-alphabet Latin↔Cyrillic transliterator. Pure Python, property-based tests, PyPI package
tasks.deliverable: pip-installable library + test suite; adopted as the frontend of every subsequent model
tasks.data_needed: None (rules + small hand-built test set); Apertium-kaz morphology as reference

tasks.task: KazVoices-500: multi-speaker TTS-grade corpus distilled from KSC2 (1.2k h, MIT) + YODAS kk subset. Pipeline: DNSMOS/NISQA quality filter (keep >3.5), pyannote diarization + speaker clustering, ASR transcript verification (reject CER>5%), loudness normalization. Target 300-500h, 500+ speakers — the dataset that makes Kazakh voice cloning trainable
tasks.deliverable: HF dataset with datasheet + filtering pipeline code; citable data paper section
tasks.data_needed: KSC2 (downloadable), YODAS kk (HF, CC); ~1TB scratch disk, GPU days for scoring (RTX 2070 feasible, slow)

tasks.task: QymyzVoice-Clone: continue-train QymyzVoice-0.6B (or IndexTTS-2) on KazVoices-500 multi-speaker data to unlock generalizing zero-shot cloning for Kazakh — fixing exactly the failure AnuarSv/IndexTTS2-Kazakh documents (single-speaker collapse)
tasks.deliverable: First open kk TTS with verified >0.7 speaker-sim on unseen speakers (KazClone-Eval); model on HF
tasks.data_needed: KazVoices-500

tasks.task: CS-300: kk-ru code-switch TTS eval + robust checkpoint. Mine 300 real code-switched sentences (social media, subtitles, forums; human-verified), benchmark all systems on CS-CER; then mitigate in QymyzVoice finetune by replaying 10-15% Russian TTS data (open ru corpora, e.g. Common Voice ru) so the Qwen3-TTS base's native Russian survives the kk finetune
tasks.deliverable: CS-300 eval set on HF + CS leaderboard column + CS-robust model checkpoint; first artifact anywhere addressing kk-ru synthesis
tasks.data_needed: 300 mined+verified CS sentences; open Russian speech data for replay

tasks.task: Latin-script TTS: first TTS accepting the official 2021 Latin alphabet. Route A (days): qazaq-tts-norm transliterates Latin→Cyrillic at the frontend. Route B (experiment): mix 15% Latin-transliterated text into the QymyzVoice finetune and compare CER. Ship as a toggle in the demo Space
tasks.deliverable: Demo: 'type Latin Kazakh, hear speech' + a paragraph-sized experimental result for the paper
tasks.data_needed: Transliteration rules (official 2021 alphabet spec); no new audio

All ingredients verified available and open-licensed; the bench is a one-week RTX 2070 job that makes every future kk TTS cite you, and the 0.6B model mirrors the QymyzLM-vs-Qwen3-0.6B paper narrative in speech — one benchmark artifact, one model artifact, both firsts.

en_zh_sota.name: Whisper-large-v3 / large-v3-turbo (OpenAI)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1.55B / 809M params; ~4.8% WER English; Apache-2.0. On Kazakh zero-shot it collapses: 56.5/47.7 normalized WER on Common Voice kk, 33.1/21.0 on FLEURS kk, 58.9/81.2 on KSC2 (large-v3 / turbo respectively)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The de-facto multilingual base everyone fine-tunes; the 5-10x gap between its EN and kk WER is the sector's core measurement

en_zh_sota.name: FireRedASR-LLM / FireRedASR-AED (FireRed, China)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 8.3B LLM variant: 3.05% avg CER Mandarin (SOTA), 1.73% WER LibriSpeech test-clean; AED variant 1.1B: 3.18% CER; Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Shows what an 'industrial-grade open model for one language' looks like — the target pattern for a national-language ASR effort, incl. singing-lyrics robustness

en_zh_sota.name: Paraformer-large + FunASR stack (Alibaba)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1.68% CER AISHELL-1, 2.85% AISHELL-2; non-autoregressive, streaming variant, ships with VAD + punctuation + ITN in one toolkit; Apache-2.0-ish model license
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The full production pipeline pattern (ASR+VAD+punct+ITN+streaming) that Kazakh completely lacks

en_zh_sota.name: NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3
en_zh_sota.numbers: 600M params, 6.34% avg WER on HF Open ASR Leaderboard at RTFx ~3,333 (≈3,300x realtime); 25 European languages (no kk); CC-BY-4.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Proves a 0.6B streaming-capable FastConformer-TDT can be near-SOTA and ultra-fast — the exact architecture recipe for a first neural streaming kk model

en_zh_sota.name: NVIDIA Canary-1B-v2
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1B params, multitask ASR+speech-translation across 25 languages, timestamps, punctuation+capitalization native; CC-BY-4.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The multitask (ASR+AST+punct) single-model bar; kk is absent from its language list

en_zh_sota.name: ElevenLabs Scribe v1 / Scribe v2 Realtime
en_zh_sota.numbers: Commercial SOTA claim across 99 languages (96.7% acc EN); Kazakh officially in their 'High Accuracy' band (5-10% WER, vendor claim, unverified independently); v2 Realtime ~150ms latency
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The commercial bar for kk that open models must beat; also the only realtime commercial API claiming good kk quality

en_zh_sota.name: Meta Omnilingual ASR (Nov 2025)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 7B-LLM flagship + smaller variants, 1,600+ languages incl. Kazakh, CER<10 for 78% of languages; Apache-2.0 code + open models
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Newest massively-multilingual baseline that any kk leaderboard must include; its kk-specific WER is unmeasured publicly — free paper material

en_zh_sota.name: pyannote speaker-diarization-3.1 / community-1
en_zh_sota.numbers: ~10% DER on standard benchmarks, language-agnostic, MIT; the default open diarization stack
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Diarization bar; never evaluated on Kazakh broadcast/podcast audio — zero kk diarization benchmarks exist

en_zh_sota.name: WhisperX + HF Open ASR Leaderboard (as ecosystem patterns)
en_zh_sota.numbers: WhisperX: 70x-realtime long-form with word-level timestamps via forced alignment + VAD; Open ASR Leaderboard: frozen normalization protocol, multilingual + long-form tracks added 2025
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The two ecosystem artifacts (long-form pipeline, public leaderboard with frozen text normalization) whose Kazakh equivalents simply do not exist

kazakh_existing.name: Speech Recognition and Synthesis Models and Platforms for the Kazakh Language (survey, Information 16(10):879, Oct 2025)
kazakh_existing.status: USABLE as prior-art for the atlas — a recent narrative survey of kk speech tech; it is NOT data-driven (no unified re-evaluation), which is the author's differentiator

gaps.gap: No public Kazakh ASR leaderboard and no frozen normalization protocol — every model self-reports on differently-normalized splits (KSC2 lowercase/no-punct vs CV/FLEURS cased/punctuated, homoglyphs, Latin digits in FLEURS), so numbers like 9.16%, 10.62%, 8.73% are mutually incomparable
gaps.why: Without a shared measuring stick nothing else in the sector can be claimed or improved honestly; the March-2026 songs paper had to build its own ad-hoc normalization just to compare 3 models. This is the cheapest field-defining artifact available

gaps.gap: No dedicated kk-ru code-switch ASR benchmark with language-tagged references, despite code-switching being the default speech register in Kazakhstan
gaps.why: KSC2 contains some CS utterances but they are not isolated, tagged, or scored separately; no model card reports CS performance; Yandex claims 'mixed kk-ru' support with zero public evidence

gaps.gap: Spontaneous/conversational speech WER is 2-4x worse than read speech and untargeted: best open model scores 5.0 on crowdsourced read speech but 18.8 on podcasts and 13.7 on talkshows (KSC2 domains)
gaps.why: Real products (meeting notes, voice assistants, subtitles) live in the spontaneous domain; no conversational training corpus exists and nobody is pseudo-labeling the abundant kk YouTube/podcast audio at scale

gaps.gap: No modern neural streaming ASR for Kazakh — the only streaming option is Kaldi-era Vosk (2022 architecture), which degrades out-of-domain (13-21 WER on FLEURS)
gaps.why: Live captioning, voice input, and call-center analytics all require <500ms streaming; the Parakeet-TDT recipe proves 0.6B streaming models can be near-SOTA, and 1,128h of KSC2 is enough data to train one

gaps.gap: No open punctuation/capitalization model and no ITN (inverse text normalization) whatsoever for Kazakh ASR output — the one punctuation paper (F1 96.75) released no model; numerals/dates/currency ITN for an agglutinative language (case-inflected numerals) has never been built openly
gaps.why: Raw lowercase unpunctuated Cyrillic is unusable for subtitles, minutes, and downstream NLP; this single missing layer blocks every kk transcription product

gaps.gap: No long-form/diarization benchmark or pipeline for Kazakh — pyannote has never been evaluated on kk broadcast audio; no WhisperX-equivalent with word timestamps exists
gaps.why: Long-form is where subtitle and meeting products operate; the components are language-agnostic and cheap to assemble, so the gap is mostly integration + a small eval set

gaps.gap: Common Voice kk is effectively dead (2.39 validated hours, 193 speakers) — no community data flywheel exists, and the CV kk test set is proverbs-heavy and unrepresentative
gaps.why: All open data is single-institution (ISSAI); demographic/dialect/children/elderly diversity has no growth channel, which caps long-term robustness

sectors.flagship_opportunity: KazASR-Bench — a public, frozen-normalization Kazakh ASR leaderboard (read / spontaneous-domain / code-switch / hallucination tracks) scoring every open fine-tune AND the commercial APIs (ElevenLabs, Yandex) that have never been independently measured on kk. It is inference-only (a week of solo work, ~$20 of API credits), instantly becomes the citation anchor every future kk ASR paper and model card must reference, converts today's incomparable self-reported numbers (9.16% vs 10.62% vs 8.73% on different normalizations) into a real ranking, and hands the survey its data-driven backbone for the speech chapter — exactly the 'genealogical, first-of-kind' positioning the paper needs.

en_zh_sota.name: OpenAI gpt-realtime / GPT-Realtime-2 (Realtime API)
en_zh_sota.numbers: $32/1M audio input tokens, $64/1M output (~$0.06/min in, $0.24/min out); production E2E latency 400-600ms; May 7 2026 added GPT-Realtime-2, GPT-Realtime-Translate ($0.034/min), GPT-Realtime-Whisper ($0.017/min). Closed/API-only.
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The commercial bar for native speech-to-speech voice agents: instruction following, tool calls, mid-sentence language switching. Kazakh support is nominal at best (voice mode claims 50+ languages; kk quality unverified — uncertain).

en_zh_sota.name: Moshi (Kyutai)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 7B temporal transformer + Mimi codec (24kHz -> 12.5Hz, 1.1kbps, 80ms frame); 160ms theoretical / ~200ms practical latency on an L4 GPU; weights CC-BY; English only.
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The open full-duplex bar — proves a small lab can ship a real-time speech-text foundation model. Its 'inner monologue' (text tokens alongside audio) is the architecture a future kk duplex model would copy.

en_zh_sota.name: Hibiki / Hibiki-M (Kyutai)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 2B backbone + 1B on-device variant; simultaneous S2ST, French->English ONLY; models CC-BY-4.0, code MIT/Apache; runs real-time on smartphones (Hibiki-M).
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The template for per-language-pair simultaneous S2ST at academic scale — exactly the recipe shape a kk<->en/ru streaming translator would follow. Shows one pair is a shippable unit.

en_zh_sota.name: Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B (Alibaba)
en_zh_sota.numbers: Apache-2.0; MoE Thinker-Talker; 211ms audio-only latency (507ms audio-video); 119 text languages, 19 speech-input, 10 speech-output. Russian in both speech lists; Kazakh in NEITHER.
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Open-weights omni SOTA (32/36 audio benchmarks). Its language lists are the hardest evidence of the Kazakh hole: even the most multilingual open speech model has zero kk speech support.

en_zh_sota.name: CosyVoice 2 / CosyVoice 3 (Alibaba FunAudioLLM)
en_zh_sota.numbers: CosyVoice2-0.5B: streaming, 150ms first-packet latency, Apache-2.0. CosyVoice3: 1.5B, trained on 1M hours, 9 languages + 18 Chinese dialects. No Kazakh.
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The LLM-based streaming-TTS bar and the single most practical fine-tune target for a first streaming, zero-shot-cloning Kazakh TTS (0.5B fits an RTX 2070 workflow).

en_zh_sota.name: SeamlessM4T-v2-large (Meta)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 2.3B, CC-BY-NC-4.0; 101 speech-input languages, 96 text, 35 speech-output. Kazakh: speech+text INPUT and text OUTPUT only — kk is NOT among the 35 S2ST speech-output targets.
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The massively-multilingual S2ST reference AND the precise gap statement: kk->X speech translation works today (as S2TT), X->kk speech does not exist in any open model. NC license also blocks products.

en_zh_sota.name: StreamSpeech (ICT/CAS, ACL 2024)
en_zh_sota.numbers: Unified offline + simultaneous S2ST via multi-task learning; SOTA on CVSS (fr/es/de->en); open code.
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Proof that simultaneous S2ST is trainable at academic compute with the right multi-task recipe — the methodological reference for a kk simul-ST probe.

en_zh_sota.name: Kyutai Unmute + Kyutai STT/TTS (July 2025)
en_zh_sota.numbers: Fully open cascade voice-agent stack: STT-1B (en/fr) 500ms delay cut to ~125ms with the flush trick (STT runs ~4x real-time); TTS 1.6B streaming (delayed-streams modeling); E2E ~450ms (multi-GPU) to ~750ms (single L40S).
en_zh_sota.why_reference: THE blueprint for the QymyzLM cascade agent: same architecture (streaming STT -> text LLM -> streaming TTS), published latency engineering tricks, all open source.

en_zh_sota.name: Sesame CSM-1B
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1B, Apache-2.0; Llama backbone + Mimi RVQ audio decoder; trained on 1M hours; blind listeners could not distinguish short clips from humans.
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The open conversational-TTS bar and a fine-tunable backbone candidate for Kazakh conversational voice (tests whether Mimi tokens transfer to kk phonology).

gaps.gap: No open speech-native LLM (omni/duplex) supports Kazakh at all — Qwen3-Omni: 19 speech-in / 10 speech-out languages, kk in neither; Moshi is English-only; nothing kk full-duplex exists even as a paper.
gaps.why: The entire 'voice-native model' paradigm (the GPT-realtime/Moshi tier) simply skips Kazakh. Until someone attaches kk speech I/O to an LLM, kk voice AI is capped at cascade architectures.

gaps.gap: No X->Kazakh speech output in any open S2ST system — SeamlessM4T-v2 supports kaz only as speech-input/text-output; kk is not among its 35 speech-output targets; Hibiki is fr->en only.
gaps.why: Speech translation INTO Kazakh (the direction that serves kk speakers consuming global content) cannot be built from any open checkpoint today; only closed apps (Soyle/MangiSoz) approximate it via internal cascades.

gaps.gap: No dedicated kk speech-translation evaluation set — only FLEURS' ~12h of generic read sentences; no CVSS/CoVoST-style kk pair, no conversational or code-switched ST eval.
gaps.why: What can't be measured doesn't get built: nobody can rank SeamlessM4T vs Whisper+NLLB vs MangiSoz for kk, so there is no leaderboard pressure and no publishable progress metric.

gaps.gap: No open streaming/expressive/zero-shot-cloning kk TTS — Piper kk voices and mms-tts-kaz are sentence-level VITS read-speech; KazEmoTTS model scores MOS 3.47-3.54; nothing in the CosyVoice2/CSM class exists for kk.
gaps.why: A voice agent is unusable without low first-packet-latency streaming TTS; this is the single component whose absence blocks every downstream kk voice product, and a 0.5B Apache-licensed fine-tune target (CosyVoice2) already exists.

gaps.gap: No open conversational/spontaneous kk speech corpus — KSC2 (1.2k h) is read/broadcast/parliament speech; zero open dialogue audio, zero duplex recordings, code-switching present but unannotated.
gaps.why: Voice agents trained/evaluated on broadcast register fail on real speech; every EN/ZH conversational model (Moshi, CSM) leaned on massive spontaneous dialogue data that kk simply lacks.

gaps.gap: No published latency/quality numbers for any kk voice pipeline — Soyle, MangiSoz, Alisa and Freedom publish no WER/MOS/latency; the only public quality datum is a vendor's '89% kk vs 95% ru' call-center claim.
gaps.why: The ecosystem has products but no engineering reference points; a single honest latency-budget table on consumer hardware would instantly become the citable baseline.

gaps.gap: No spoken-language-understanding benchmark for kk — no audio KazMMLU, no VoiceBench-style agent eval, so 'does the assistant understand spoken Kazakh' is unanswerable.
gaps.why: Cheap to create (TTS + human spot-check over existing KazMMLU) and it converts the SLM's text benchmark story into a voice story.

gaps.gap: License friction on the best multilingual assets — SeamlessM4T-v2 and mms-tts-kaz are CC-BY-NC; the commercially-clean kk stack (CC-BY KSC2/KazakhTTS2 + Apache Whisper/CosyVoice/CSM) exists in pieces but has never been assembled and documented.
gaps.why: Product builders default to Russian cloud APIs because nobody has published a 'commercially safe open kk voice stack' reference.

sectors.sector: speech-to-speech (real-time voice agents + speech-to-speech translation) for Kazakh
sectors.flagship_opportunity: Ship the first open real-time Kazakh voice stack — a documented sub-1.5s cascade (whisper-turbo-ksc2 -> QymyzLM-500M -> streaming kk TTS from a CosyVoice2-0.5B fine-tune) with published per-stage latency numbers on consumer hardware, plus the first kk speech-translation eval set. en_zh_sota.numbers: 10.7B T5 encoder-decoder, 419 languages incl. kk, trained on 250B tokens, Apache 2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The other permissively-licensed massively-multilingual MT baseline covering kk; its document-level audited dataset (MADLAD-400) also contains a kk monolingual split usable for CPT

en_zh_sota.name: Tower v2 / Tower+ (Unbabel-IST)
en_zh_sota.numbers: WMT24 General MT winner: ranked 1st on ALL language pairs; 7B variant beat GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, DeepL; recipe = CPT on multilingual+parallel data, MT SFT, quality-aware decoding (MBR/TRR over 100 samples from 70B)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The canonical 'MT-tune an LLM' recipe and proof that mid-size open models beat closed APIs when specialized — the exact playbook to port to a 600M Kazakh SLM (no Kazakh in Tower's 22 languages = open lane)

en_zh_sota.name: X-ALMA (ICLR 2025)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 13B, 50 languages incl. Kazakh (Group 8: en/az/kk/ky/tr/uz/ar/he/fa Turkic+ module); plug-and-play per-group modules + Adaptive-Rejection Preference Optimization; beats Aya-101/Aya-23 on every FLORES-200 direction by COMET-22
en_zh_sota.why_reference: SOTA open LLM-MT that explicitly covers Kazakh via a Turkic module — must-beat baseline for any new kk model; ARPO is the preference-tuning method to copy at small scale (its predecessor ALMA-R showed CPO works with only ~20K pairs)

en_zh_sota.name: Qwen3-MT (qwen-mt-turbo API)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 92 languages (Kazakh not explicitly confirmed in coverage list — uncertain), MoE, $0.50/M output tokens, launched July 2025; productized terminology control, translation memory, domain prompts
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The bar for PRODUCT features (terminology injection, domain control) that no Kazakh MT system offers; also the cheap synthetic-data teacher for zh-side directions

en_zh_sota.name: GPT-4/Gemini-class LLM MT on Kazakh (measured)
en_zh_sota.numbers: SIGTURK 2024 'Do LLMs Speak Kazakh?': FLORES kk→en BLEU — Google Translate 0.35 > GPT-4 0.29 > YaGPT3 0.23 > Gemini 1.5 Pro 0.22 (Gemini returned empty for ~36-38% of kk inputs); Llama-2 ≈ 0.00
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Hard evidence that frontier LLMs still trail a dedicated MT system on Kazakh generation — the exact gap a specialized small model can exploit; needs re-measuring on the 2026 model wave

en_zh_sota.name: WMT22 CometKiwi-DA (reference-free QE)
en_zh_sota.numbers: Unbabel/wmt22-cometkiwi-da — quality-estimation model whose HF language tags include kk; standard filter for synthetic bitext pipelines
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The tooling bar for data quality: modern MT data engines (NLLB, MADLAD, Hunyuan) all COMET-QE-filter their bitext; whether its kk scores actually correlate with human judgment is unvalidated — itself a gap

en_zh_sota.name: Doc-level / paragraph-level MT (WMT24+ standard)
en_zh_sota.numbers: WMT24 General MT moved to paragraph-level evaluation; Tower v2 and Hunyuan-MT trained with document context; terminology + doc-level are the two WMT-track capabilities defining 'modern MT' vs 2020-era sentence MT
en_zh_sota.why_reference: For en/zh, sentence-level MT is a solved commodity and the frontier is documents + constraints; every Kazakh resource (KazParC, FLORES) is sentence-level — a full capability tier missing

kazakh_existing.name: KazParC corpus (ISSAI, LREC-COLING 2024)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable — the anchor corpus. 371,902 human-assisted parallel sentences across kk/en/ru/tr (kk-en 363.6k, kk-ru 363.5k pairs); domains: mass media 32.4%, general 25.5%, legal 20.8%, education/science 12.4%, fiction 8.9%; plus SynC: 1,797,066 synthetic sentences machine-translated via Google Translate (distillation-ceiling + ToS-gray). CC BY 4.0.

kazakh_existing.name: Tilmash (issai/tilmash)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable but aging (uploaded Oct 2023, no update found through Jul 2026; 882 monthly downloads). NLLB-200-1.3B fine-tuned on KazParC+SynC. KazParC test BLEU|chrF: kk→en 0.32|0.62 (edges Google 0.31), but en→kk 0.21|0.60 LOSES to Google 0.30|0.65; kk↔ru ≈ parity with Yandex. Licensing note for atlas: released CC BY 4.0 although base NLLB is CC-BY-NC — inconsistent.

kazakh_existing.name: deepvk kazRush-kk-ru / kazRush-ru-kk (VK)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable — only from-scratch small models: ~197M T5, trained on open parallel data (2024), Apache 2.0. ru↔kk only. The natural size-class baseline for a 500-600M SLM on kk-ru.

kazakh_existing.name: Tencent Hy-MT2-7B / Hy-MT2-1.8B / HY-MT1.5-1.8B
kazakh_existing.status: Usable, UNBENCHMARKED on kk — tagged kk among 33 languages, Apache 2.0, 24k-112k monthly downloads. Likely current open SOTA for Kazakh but zero published kk FLORES/KazParC numbers; script coverage (Cyrillic vs China-Kazakh Arabic) unverified. Verification = quick win.

kazakh_existing.name: NLLB-200 / MADLAD-400 / X-ALMA / mBART-50 (kk coverage)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable multilingual baselines covering kaz_Cyrl; NLLB is CC-BY-NC; X-ALMA-Group8 has a dedicated Turkic module with kk; nobody has published a side-by-side kk comparison of these against Tilmash/commercial APIs.

kazakh_existing.name: Karpov 2026 — synthetic+original systems for Bashkir/Kazakh/Kyrgyz/Tatar/Chuvash (EACL 2026 LoResMT)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable and current: NLLB-200-distilled-600M + LoRA on synthetic data reaches chrF++ 49.71 for Kazakh (ru→kk); dataset + weights released, CC BY 4.0. Direct evidence a 600M model is competitive on kk — the existence proof for the QymyzLM MT question.

kazakh_existing.name: Google Translate / Yandex Translate (+19 other commercial APIs)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable, closed. 21 commercial engines support kk (Google, Yandex, Microsoft, DeepL, Baidu, Amazon, Qwen-MT...). Google is still the strongest measured system: FLORES kk→en BLEU 0.35; KazParC en→kk 0.30. Yandex ≈ Google on kk↔ru. No public doc-level or terminology features for kk.

kazakh_existing.name: Eval sets: FLORES-200/FLORES+ (kaz_Cyrl), NTREX-128, Belebele-kk, KazParC test, WMT19 newstest kk-en
kazakh_existing.status: Usable but all sentence-level; FLORES kk side is translationese (noted in SIGTURK); WMT19 kk-en newstest + crawl corpus is the historical anchor (UMD system +5.45 BLEU via transfer learning/back-translation, 2019). No doc-level, terminology, or code-switch eval exists.

kazakh_existing.name: Apertium-kaz (+apertium-eng-kaz, kaz-tat)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable as morphology, outdated as MT: the kaz morphological transducer/disambiguator is maintained and valuable (free analyzer for terminology/inflection work), but the eng-kaz translation pair remains incubator-stage; research activity mostly 2013-2021.

kazakh_existing.name: Nothingger/kaz-literature-translation + kaz-rus-eng-literature-parallel-corpus
kazakh_existing.status: Claim-only model (Tilmash fine-tune, no metrics, ~10 downloads) but the dataset is real: 71.1k literary kk-ru-en parallel examples (Jul 2024, Apache 2.0) — one of very few domain-specific kk bitexts.

kazakh_existing.name: OPUS kk-en/kk-ru bitext
kazakh_existing.status: Usable with caveats: ~1M kk-en pairs on OPUS, but per published analysis topics are 'seriously restricted' and quality 'shallow'; needs COMET-QE filtering before use.

kazakh_existing.name: Termincom.kz — republican terminology database
kazakh_existing.status: Usable raw resource, never operationalized for MT: ~21,000 government-approved kk terms (40.8% native, 59.2% borrowed/mixed) from the state terminology commission; no ML-ready export, no glossary-constrained MT built on it.

kazakh_existing.name: Kazakh MT academic tail 2025-2026
kazakh_existing.source: https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/15/3126 (kk-en-ru IT-domain NLLB fine-tuning, Aug 2025), https://doi.org/10.3390/a19030199 (fine-tuned GPT-4.1-mini post-editing of kk translations: 0.84 vs 0.80 human-rated, Mar 2026), https://doi.org/10.3390/computers15020073 (Turkic MT adaptation)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable signals, fragmented: small MDPI-tier studies, each with own test sets, no shared leaderboard; confirms activity but zero consolidation.

kazakh_existing.name: KazLLM-1.0 8B/70B (ISSAI) and Sherkala-Chat-8B (MBZUAI/Inception)
kazakh_existing.status: Usable general kk LLMs, MT-unbenchmarked: neither publishes systematic FLORES/KazParC translation scores; their MT ability vs dedicated systems is an open question the atlas can answer cheaply.

kazakh_existing.name: Dead/toy HF artifacts
kazakh_existing.status: Abandoned — documents the graveyard for the atlas's genealogy layer.

gaps.gap: No public Kazakh MT leaderboard: the 2025-26 model wave (Hy-MT2, Qwen3-MT, GPT-4o/Gemini-2.5, X-ALMA) has never been benchmarked on kk; last systematic comparison is SIGTURK 2024 with 2023-era models, and Tilmash's published numbers date to 2023
gaps.why: Nobody — including ISSAI — can currently say what SOTA for Kazakh MT is; every downstream decision (which teacher to distill, which baseline to beat) is guesswork until this exists

gaps.gap: en→kk / ru→kk generation direction is the weak side of every system: Tilmash en→kk BLEU 0.21 vs Google 0.30; LLMs measurably worse at generating Kazakh than understanding it (SIGTURK: all models drop on generative tasks; Gemini returned empty for ~1/3 of kk requests)
gaps.why: Into-Kazakh is the direction that matters for content localization, government use, and synthetic-data generation for SLM/embeddings — and it's exactly where agglutinative morphology + 4.7-4.9 tokenizer fertility hurt most

gaps.gap: Zero document-level MT resources: every kk corpus (KazParC, FLORES, OPUS) is sentence-level; no doc-aligned test set, no doc-level scores for any system
gaps.why: EN/ZH MT moved to paragraph/document evaluation at WMT24; kk lacks the entire capability tier (pronoun/ellipsis/terminology consistency across sentences), meaning real-document quality is unmeasured and likely poor

gaps.gap: No terminology-controlled MT despite Termincom's 21k state-approved terms; legal/medical kk translation quality unmeasured even though all Kazakhstan laws are published bilingually (kk/ru on adilet.zan.kz)
gaps.why: Terminology control is a paid product feature in Qwen3-MT/DeepL for en/zh; in Kazakhstan it's a legal-compliance need (official term usage is regulated) with zero open tooling — clearest standalone-product lane in the sector

gaps.gap: Parallel data is small and license/quality-compromised: 372k human KazParC pairs + ~1M shallow OPUS pairs; the largest augmentation (SynC 1.8M) is Google-Translate distillate, capping quality at Google's 2023 en→kk level and ToS-gray for commercial use
gaps.why: Modern MT recipes (Hunyuan, Tower) assume tens of millions of QE-filtered pairs; no one has rebuilt kk synthetic data with a 2026 Apache-2.0 teacher + COMET-QE filtering — this single upgrade lifts every model trained after it

gaps.gap: No modern small (<600M) open model covering kk↔en+ru: kazRush (197M) does ru↔kk only; Tilmash is 1.3B NLLB with NC-inherited license ambiguity; nothing runs on-device/edge with current-generation quality
gaps.why: 13-16M speakers with heavy mobile usage and kk/ru code-switching is an on-device MT market; also the exact niche where QymyzLM-class models can claim a defensible first

gaps.gap: kk↔zh has no dedicated open training corpus or benchmarked system (only implicit n-way FLORES eval and massively-multilingual models' pivot quality)
gaps.why: China is Kazakhstan's #1 trade partner and hosts ~1.5M ethnic Kazakhs, but the direction is servable short-term via en/ru pivoting; a first kk-zh eval is cheap because FLORES is n-way parallel

gaps.gap: Latin-script Kazakh (official transition target ~2031) is unsupported: no MT system accepts kk-Latn input, no transliteration-robustness eval exists
gaps.why: Low urgency today but a guaranteed future break; a Cyrillic↔Latin converter + robustness eval is days of work and future-proofs every other artifact

sectors.flagship_opportunity: KazMT-Bench + the model it justifies: nobody on Earth currently knows what SOTA Kazakh MT is — the last systematic comparison used 2023-era models, Tilmash's numbers are from 2023, and the strongest likely system (Tencent Hy-MT2, Apache 2.0, kk-tagged, May 2026) has zero published Kazakh scores. A one-week public leaderboard makes the author the reference point for the whole sector, and its outputs cascade directly into the two personal goals: Hy-MT2 becomes the clean-license distillation teacher for a <600M QymyzLM-MT that dethrones the aging 1.3B Tilmash (existence proof already published: NLLB-600M+LoRA hits chrF++ 49.71 on ru→kk), and the same back-translation/round-trip engine mass-produces contrastive pairs for the embedding model. One benchmark, one small model, one data engine — the sector's eval standard, its best small model, and its training-data supply chain, all owned by one solo engineer.

en_zh_sota.name: DeepSeek-OCR
en_zh_sota.numbers: 3B MoE decoder (A570M active) + DeepEncoder; ~97% OCR precision at <10x optical compression, ~60% at 20x; beats GOT-OCR2 using only 100 vision tokens/page vs 256; 200k+ pages/day on one A100-40G; open weights (HF)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Defines the 2025-26 paradigm: OCR as context compression for LLMs. The 'archive-to-tokens' framing is exactly what a Kazakh SLM pretraining pipeline needs.

en_zh_sota.name: GOT-OCR2.0
en_zh_sota.numbers: 580M params end-to-end, Apache 2.0; handles plain text, formulas, tables, sheet music; SOTA on Fox benchmark for EN/ZH PDF OCR at its size
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Proof that a sub-600M unified OCR model can be SOTA — the size class that fits the author's RTX 2070 fine-tuning budget and mirrors the QymyzLM philosophy.

en_zh_sota.name: PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5
en_zh_sota.numbers: Mobile-size det+rec pipeline, 106-111 languages, Apache 2.0; Kazakh nominally covered via shared cyrillic_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec — a Cyrillic group model trained on only ~7,600 Cyrillic text images total
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The deployable classical bar AND the cheapest adaptation target: its rec head retrains on a single consumer GPU, and its 7.6k-image Cyrillic training set shows how thin kk coverage really is.

en_zh_sota.name: PaddleOCR-VL (0.9B)
en_zh_sota.numbers: NaViT encoder + ERNIE-4.5-0.3B; 109 languages; OmniDocBench v1.5 ~94.5 (v1.6 96.33 vendor-reported); Apache 2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Sub-1B VLM doing full document parsing (layout, tables, formulas, charts) at SOTA — the architecture bar for a future 'Kazakh document parser'.

en_zh_sota.name: dots.ocr (RedNote)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1.7B single VLM for layout+content, 100+ languages, MIT; introduced XDocParse (126-language doc-parsing benchmark), SOTA across its metrics
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Best open multilingual document parser; the natural base to probe/extend for Kazakh since it already claims 100+ languages — verify whether kk is actually usable.

en_zh_sota.name: Qwen3-VL
en_zh_sota.numbers: 2B-32B dense + MoE; OCR in 32-39 languages (>70% acc on 32); 32B: OCRBench 86.9, DocVQA 93.3, ChartQA 94.0; Apache 2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The general-VLM doc-understanding bar; also the base of ISSAI's Qolda-AVL, so its kk OCR ceiling matters directly.

en_zh_sota.name: MinerU2.5
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1.2B decoupled parsing VLM; OmniDocBench 90.67, beating MonkeyOCR-pro-3B and dots.ocr at lower compute
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The practical PDF-to-markdown extraction pipeline standard for building pretraining corpora from documents — the tool class a KazNEB pipeline should emulate.

en_zh_sota.name: GLM-OCR / olmOCR-Bench ecosystem
en_zh_sota.numbers: GLM-OCR: OmniDocBench v1.5 overall 94.62 (highest); olmOCR-Bench (AllenAI) top open scores ~83 — benchmark-driven development is the norm in EN/ZH
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Shows the meta-gap: EN/ZH progress is driven by page-level benchmarks (OmniDocBench, olmOCR-Bench, Fox). Kazakh has no real-scan page-level equivalent at all.

en_zh_sota.name: KOHTD/HKR-era handwriting SOTA (TrOCR-style attention + CTC)
en_zh_sota.numbers: TrOCR (334M base) and CTC/attention recognizers are the published baselines on KOHTD/HKR; KOHTD paper reports CTC- and attention-based results on 140k word images
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The handwriting-recognition method bar that kk data already supports — fine-tuning TrOCR on KOHTD is a known-feasible recipe awaiting a public model.

kazakh_existing.name: Tesseract kaz.traineddata
kazakh_existing.status: usable but weak — official kaz model exists (Apache 2.0); older academic evaluation reports 24-28% recognition errors (~72-76% accuracy) vs ABBYY/CuneiForm; KazakhOCR (2026) confirms Tesseract handles Cyrillic kk best of the three scripts and fails on Arabic-script Kazakh. No published modern CER on real scans.

kazakh_existing.name: PaddleOCR cyrillic_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec (Kazakh in Cyrillic group)
kazakh_existing.status: claim-only for kk quality — Kazakh is listed as supported, but via a shared Cyrillic model whose recognition dataset is ~7,600 images across ALL Cyrillic languages; per-language kk accuracy (esp. Ә,Ғ,Қ,Ң,Ө,Ұ,Ү,Һ,І) never published.

kazakh_existing.name: KOHTD — Kazakh Offline Handwritten Text Dataset (2021/22)
kazakh_existing.status: usable but access-gated — 3,000 handwritten exam papers, 140,335 segmented word images, ~922,010 symbols, full 42-letter Cyrillic; non-commercial license, access via application form/email. Largest kk handwriting resource.

kazakh_existing.name: HKR — Handwritten Kazakh & Russian database (2020)
kazakh_existing.status: usable but skewed — ~1,500 forms, ~63k sentences, 715,699 symbols, ~200 writers, but only ~5% Kazakh (95% Russian); public on GitHub.

kazakh_existing.name: KazakhOCR synthetic benchmark (AbjadNLP @ EACL 2026)
kazakh_existing.status: usable, synthetic-only — 7,219 synthetic images covering all three Kazakh scripts (Arabic/Cyrillic/Latin), MIT, 15.3GB on HF (2,484 downloads). Key finding: Gemma-3-12B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Llama-3.2-11B-Vision all fail on Latin and Arabic-script Kazakh and misclassify Arabic-script kk as Arabic/Farsi/Kurdish. gaps.gap: No real-scan, page-level Kazakh OCR benchmark. Everything is synthetic (KazakhOCR 7.2k, Darmm 200k) or tiny (OCRBench-Kazakh: 199 print images). No kk equivalent of OmniDocBench/olmOCR-Bench — nobody can even measure whether Tesseract, PaddleOCR, Google Vision, or Qolda is best on a scanned Kazakh book page.
gaps.why: Without a benchmark there is no leaderboard, no way to prove any fine-tune helps, and no citable number for the atlas. EN/ZH progress (DeepSeek-OCR, GLM-OCR) is entirely benchmark-driven. This gates every other task in the sector.

gaps.gap: No open Kazakh-specific recognition model with verified quality on the 9 kk-only letters (Ә,Ғ,Қ,Ң,Ө,Ұ,Ү,Һ,І). All open engines route kk through generic Cyrillic models: Tesseract (72-76% acc in older eval), PaddleOCR (7.6k-image shared Cyrillic set), Google Vision ('mapped' to Cyrillic). Diacritic confusion with Russian Cyrillic is anecdotally the #1 failure mode but has never been quantified.
gaps.why: Kazakh-specific letters carry high semantic load in an agglutinative language; substituting Ұ→У corrupts downstream corpora, search, and any OCR-derived SLM training data.

gaps.gap: Arabic-script Kazakh (töte jazu, pre-1929 print + ~1.5M diaspora in China/Iran/Afghanistan who still use it) has zero working OCR: KazakhOCR (2026) showed all tested MLLMs and Tesseract fail, misidentifying it as Arabic/Farsi/Kurdish. No real training or eval data exists beyond synthetic renders.
gaps.why: A century of Kazakh print (newspapers like 'Qazaq' 1913-18, early books, the National Center's Arabographic manuscripts) is unreadable by machines — a nation-scale text corpus and cultural heritage locked in images.

gaps.gap: Latin-script Kazakh OCR unprepared for the ~2031 transition: no training data or eval for the 2021 31-letter Latin alphabet; MLLMs fail on Latin kk in KazakhOCR benchmark.
gaps.why: State-mandated script change means every OCR system in the country breaks by design within 5 years; whoever ships Latin-kk OCR first owns the transition.

gaps.gap: No Kazakh document-parsing / DocVQA / KIE resources: nothing for tables, forms, receipts, contracts, or eGov PDFs in kk. OCRBench-Kazakh's 142 chart-VQA pairs are the entire country's document-understanding eval. dots.ocr's XDocParse covers 126 languages — kk presence unverified.
gaps.why: Document AI (not raw OCR) is where the business value is — banks, eGov, legal. EN/ZH bar is full-page layout+table+formula parsing; kk has literally nothing measurable.

gaps.gap: Handwriting data is gated or skewed: KOHTD requires application and is non-commercial; HKR is 95% Russian; no permissively-licensed kk handwriting benchmark exists, and no open kk HTR model has ever been published despite two datasets existing since 2021.
gaps.why: The data exists but nobody shipped the model — a pure execution gap that a solo engineer can close with a TrOCR fine-tune.

gaps.gap: Archive-to-corpus pipeline missing: KazNEB's 82,853 digitized items have no open OCR text layer, and no one has published an OCR-extracted Kazakh book corpus. Meanwhile EN/ZH treats OCR as the pretraining-data pump (DeepSeek-OCR: 200k pages/day).
gaps.why: Kazakh SLMs (incl. QymyzLM) are token-starved; kk web text is thin, but a century of edited, high-quality book/newspaper prose sits un-OCR'd. This is the single largest untapped kk token source.

gaps.gap: KZ ID/form parsing exists only as closed commercial SDKs (Verigram, Smart Engines); no open synthetic KZ document dataset or field-extraction model.
gaps.why: Commercial products serve the market adequately; open work here is a product opportunity more than a research gap, and carries PII/security-feature sensitivities.

gaps.gap: No morphology-aware Kazakh analyzer in any mainstream search engine: ES/OpenSearch built-ins, official Snowball, PostgreSQL FTS, Meilisearch all lack kk; the only artifact is an abandoned 2018 plugin for ES 5.6
gaps.why: BM25 is half of every hybrid RAG stack, and for an agglutinative language unstemmed BM25 silently loses recall (each noun can surface in dozens of suffixed forms). The Apr-2026 legal RAG paper shows BM25 still contributes +5.5pp inside hybrid — the sparse leg matters and is currently crippled. Fixable by one engineer; apertium-kaz and TurkicNLP already provide the morphology.

gaps.gap: Zero Kazakh rerankers and zero kk-tagged embedding models on Hugging Face (verified via HF API, Jul 2026)
gaps.why: Every kk RAG deployment (including government agents) runs multilingual models zero-shot with unmeasured kk quality; the informatics_kaz study shows multilingual embedders at only 0.59-0.63 Accuracy@1. The reranker slot is completely empty — first-mover with a 100M-class open model wins the whole niche.

gaps.gap: Kazakh is invisible in MTEB/MMTEB: no kk retrieval or reranking task despite KazQAD existing since 2024 with ready-made qrels
gaps.why: Model developers optimize what leaderboards measure. Until KazQAD is an MTEB task, no frontier embedding release will ever report or care about kk numbers — and the user's own embedding model has no public arena to win.

gaps.gap: No Kazakh RAG evaluation harness: RAGAS prompts are English, no validated kk LLM-judge, both 2025-26 kk RAG papers hand-rolled incompatible eval setups
gaps.why: Without a shared eval, 'best kk RAG' claims are unfalsifiable and every team re-invents evaluation. This is also the cheapest field-defining artifact: the components (KazQAD, KazMMLU, legal QA pairs) already exist.

gaps.gap: No public training triples with hard negatives for kk retrieval — only KazQAD's 12k qrels plus 61k noisy machine-translated NQ triples
gaps.why: This is the direct blocker for training both the best-on-market kk embedder and any reranker above toy scale. EN/ZH SOTA (BGE, Qwen3-Embedding) is built on hundreds of millions of mined pairs; kk has essentially none.

gaps.gap: kk/ru code-switched query handling does not exist anywhere in the stack (no test set, no rewriter, no analyzer support)
gaps.why: Real Kazakhstani users mix kk/ru inside a single query; a kk-only or ru-only index misses half the formulations. Every production system (eGov agents, bank support bots) hits this on day one, and there is not even a benchmark to measure the damage.

gaps.gap: No kk multi-hop QA data or agentic-search baseline (Search-R1/DeepResearch-class work has no kk counterpart)
gaps.why: Agentic RAG is where EN/ZH is heading; kk lacks even the eval set. Lower urgency than the retrieval layer, but a cheap dataset now positions the atlas as forward-looking.

gaps.gap: KazQAD's passage corpus is a frozen ~2022 Wikipedia snapshot; no maintained, chunked, RAG-ready kk corpus exists
gaps.why: Everyone rebuilding kk-wiki preprocessing from scratch wastes effort and makes results incomparable; a refreshed 2026 corpus (244k articles) is a days-level task that standardizes the substrate.

sectors.flagship_opportunity: Ship the "KazRAG stack" — the missing retrieval layer for an entire national language, as one coherent release: morphology-aware BM25 analyzer (ES/OpenSearch plugin + upstreamed Snowball stemmer), the FIRST open Kazakh reranker, KazQAD contributed to MTEB, and KazRAGBench (validated kk RAGAS). Every Kazakh RAG deployment today — including Kazakhstan's government eGov AI agents scaling to 7M users by end-2026 — runs on unadapted multilingual components with literally zero kk-specific retrieval models on Hugging Face (verified Jul 2026) and no way to measure kk quality. The pieces are cheap (KazQAD qrels, apertium-kaz morphology, an 84M Apache-2.0 encoder base all exist), the demand is state-scale, the niche is empty, and whoever plants the benchmark + reranker flag defines the field and becomes the default dependency of every kk RAG product — while feeding the embedding goal its training data, its leaderboard, and its eval harness.

gaps.gap: Zero open Kazakh preference/DPO data. The only large alignment corpora (Sherkala 3.5M kk pairs, KazLLM's SFT) are closed; the one kk DPO paper explicitly worked around the absence with loss regularization.
gaps.why: Without preference pairs, no open kk model can run the DPO/RLHF stage that separates 2023-era chat models from modern ones; every kk SLM (SozKZ, QymyzLM, Til-Core) is stuck at SFT-only. First open set defines the field.

gaps.gap: Open kk instruction data is translationese-dominated and tiny: largest open set is 52k machine-translated Alpaca; largest native-context set is 10.6k GPT-4o synthetic. No native-curated COIG-CQIA-style corpus, no Magpie run on the existing aligned kk 8Bs.
gaps.why: SFT quality ceiling: models learn calqued Russian/English syntax instead of natural Kazakh; Sherkala proved 3.5M pairs work but kept them private, so the open ecosystem trains on ~1-2% of that volume at lower quality.

gaps.gap: No Kazakh safety classifier exists — no LlamaGuard/ShieldGemma equivalent, only eval prompt sets (Qorǵau, KZ-SafetyPrompts) and small academic hate-speech corpora. Llama Guard 3's 8 languages exclude kk.
gaps.why: No kk LLM can be deployed with moderation today; Qorǵau already showed multilingual models behave inconsistently in kk and worse on kk-ru code-switching, so English guards silently fail.

gaps.gap: No live human-preference evaluation: kz-transformers' offline arena is asleep, their leaderboard ranks only closed API models, and no kk model has ever received crowd Elo votes.
gaps.why: All kk model comparisons rest on translated MCQ benchmarks; nobody knows which model native speakers actually prefer — the single most cited signal in EN/ZH (LMArena, 6.8M votes) has no kk analogue.

gaps.gap: No contamination-safe eval protocol: KazMMLU and the entire ISSAI translated-benchmark suite sit on HF with answers public, no canary strings, no held-out split, no overlap audits against kk pretraining corpora (MDBKD 24M texts, CC).
gaps.why: Any claimed KazMMLU gain (including QymyzLM's target of beating Qwen3-0.6B's 32.8%) is rebuttable as leakage; the paper's headline claim is undefendable without this.

gaps.gap: No meta-evaluation of LLM-as-judge / reward models in Kazakh — nobody has measured whether GPT-4o/Claude/Gemini judgments agree with native speakers on kk outputs (MM-Eval-style, kk not covered).
gaps.why: Every synthetic-preference and arena-lite plan depends on a judge; if judges are unreliable in kk (plausible given tokenizer fertility 4.7-4.9 and translationese blindness), the whole preference pipeline built on them is noise.

gaps.gap: Extreme fragmentation: 20+ micro-datasets across personal HF accounts with no unified schema, quality labels, dedup, or discovery — most have <30 downloads.
gaps.why: Effort duplication and invisibility; a curated 'Tulu-kk mixture' + atlas page would make the existing scattered work usable overnight.

gaps.gap: License trap on anchors: KazMMLU is CC-BY-NC-4.0 and Sherkala is CC-BY-NC-SA — non-commercial terms leak into anything derived from them.
gaps.why: A product-first builder must generate/curate commercially-clean alternatives (Apache-2.0/CC-BY) or the eventual products can't legally use the ecosystem's best assets.

en_zh_sota.name: Qwen3-VL family (Alibaba)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 2B/4B/8B/32B dense + 30B-A3B/235B-A22B MoE; released Sep-Oct 2025; MMBench-EN 89.3 (235B-A22B), 2B thinking 79.9 -> 8B 85.3; RealWorldQA 79.2; image+video+OCR in 30+ languages; Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The full-spectrum open bar: one family from 2B edge to frontier MoE, covering VQA, charts, OCR, video. The 2B/4B tier is what a Kazakh VLM must be measured against.

en_zh_sota.name: InternVL3.5 (OpenGVLab)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 1B/2B/4B/8B/14B/38B dense + 20B-A4B/30B-A3B/241B-A28B MoE; 4B avg 79.7 across 9 benchmarks (MMBench, MMStar, AI2D, OCRBench, MathVista...); Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The InternViT-300M + LLM recipe that ISSAI's Qolda is literally built on (InternVL3_5-4B base) — the adaptation-friendly architecture for low-resource languages.

en_zh_sota.name: SmolVLM / SmolVLM2 (HuggingFace)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 256M/500M/2.2B; 500M: OCRBench 61.0, DocVQA 70.5, AI2D 59.2, runs in 1.2GB VRAM; 256M in 0.8GB; SmolVLM2 adds video; Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Existence proof that a ~500M text backbone + SigLIP makes a usable VLM — the exact template for QymyzVLM on the author's <=600M SLM, and it fits an RTX 2070 for inference.

en_zh_sota.name: Qwen2.5-VL (3B/7B/72B)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 3B/7B/72B, Feb 2025 (arXiv 2502.13923); 7B-Instruct was evaluated on KazakhOCR and failed Kazakh Latin and Arabic scripts entirely; Apache-2.0 (3B: Qwen license)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The most-deployed open VLM baseline of 2025; its documented failure on Kazakh scripts (KazakhOCR paper) is the concrete gap statement for the atlas.

en_zh_sota.name: Gemma 3 (Google, 4B/12B/27B multimodal)
en_zh_sota.numbers: SigLIP vision encoder, 128K context, text side covers 140+ languages; Gemma-3-12B-it also failed Kazakh Latin/Arabic OCR in KazakhOCR eval; Gemma license (commercial-friendly)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The multilingual small-VLM bar — best open multilingual text coverage attached to vision, yet still weak on Kazakh script specifics; a Kazakh adapter on Gemma-3-4B is the obvious mid-size competitor to beat or use.

en_zh_sota.name: PaliGemma 2 (Google)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 3B/10B/28B = SigLIP-So400m + Gemma 2; transfer-learning-first design, SOTA on captioning/OCR transfer at 3B (arXiv 2412.03555); uncertain: not re-verified this session, training-data knowledge
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The canonical 'frozen-ish SigLIP + small LM, 2-3 stage alignment' recipe with published stage hyperparameters — the training playbook for a Kazakh SigLIP+SLM build.

en_zh_sota.name: ALM-Bench (MBZUAI, CVPR 2025)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 100 languages incl. Kazakh (Cyrillic), 22.7K QA total (~228/language), 19 cultural categories, 800+ hours native-annotator verification; CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The bar for culturally-grounded multilingual VLM eval — and currently the ONLY native-verified Kazakh VQA data in existence (~228 items, non-commercial license).

en_zh_sota.name: CVQA (NeurIPS 2024)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 26 languages / 33 country-language pairs, ~9K culturally-grounded MCQ VQA; Kazakh NOT included (verified in Table 8; only Mongolian from the region)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The community-extensible cultural VQA pattern; its verified Kazakh absence is both a gap citation for the atlas and a concrete contribution target.

Kazakh vision scores vs InternVL3.5-4B baseline: AI2D-kk 67.62 vs 51.42, MMStar-kk 56.53 vs 49.33, RealWorldQA-kk 57.07 vs 38.74, KazakhOCR 60.54 vs 30.81. GGUF variant exists (issai/Qolda_GGUF). gaps.gap: No open Kazakh vision-language TRAINING corpus (captions or visual instructions). ISSAI's Oylan corpus (10M images / 50M QA) is closed; verified full issai HF inventory contains only eval benchmarks; nothing else exists on HF/GitHub.
gaps.why: Nobody outside ISSAI can train or even fine-tune a kk VLM today. Whoever releases the first open corpus sets the ecosystem default — this is the single highest-leverage artifact.

gaps.gap: No open Kazakh VLM under 1B params. Smallest open kk VLM is Qolda 4.3B (needs ~9GB+ even quantized); SmolVLM proves 500M works (1.2GB VRAM).
gaps.why: Edge/on-device (the stated Qolda motivation!) and cheap-inference products are locked out; also this is exactly the QymyzLM backbone opportunity — a 0.6B kk VLM has no competitor.

gaps.gap: Kazakh VLM evaluation is ~100% machine-translated (all 8 ISSAI suites); the only native cultural VQA is ALM-Bench's ~228 items under a non-commercial license; CVQA has no Kazakh split (verified).
gaps.why: MT benchmarks reward translationese and miss cultural grounding + kk/ru code-switching; there is no commercially-usable native eval, so all reported 'Kazakh VLM' numbers measure translation robustness, not Kazakh understanding.

gaps.gap: Real-world Kazakh text-in-image understanding is unmeasured: KazakhOCR is synthetic-only; no scene-text (signage/storefront), receipt, or document-VQA dataset with real photos exists; VLMs verifiably fail Kazakh Latin/Arabic scripts and classical OCR still beats MLLMs on kk CER.
gaps.why: Text-in-image is the #1 practical VLM use (documents, eGov, signage) and the 2031 Latin transition makes the failure mode a national-scale product risk; nobody has real-world numbers.

gaps.gap: No public leaderboard: frontier models (Qwen3-VL, Gemma 3, InternVL3.5, GPT-4o/Gemini) have never been publicly scored on the new ISSAI kk multimodal suites — only Qolda-vs-its-own-baseline numbers exist.
gaps.why: Cheap to fix and high-visibility: without it no one (including ISSAI) knows if Qolda actually beats stock Qwen3-VL-4B on Kazakh.

gaps.gap: No Kazakh meme / social-media multimodal dataset (kk/ru code-switching in images+text). Verified: zero results; nearest analogs are Bengali/Tamil meme datasets.
gaps.why: Code-switching is the default register of Kazakhstani social media; moderation/analytics products have no data, and it is the hardest realistic test of kk VLM robustness.

gaps.gap: Kazakh video-language and image-text retrieval are unmeasured: no kk video-QA data (Oylan closed; sign-language datasets are the only video), and no kk image-text retrieval benchmark for CLIP-family models (jina-clip-v2's 89 languages: kk support unverified/undocumented).
gaps.why: Retrieval is the direct bridge to the author's embedding goal (a kk CLIP text tower is a natural extension of the best kk text embedder); video is the next wave arriving with zero kk data.
