sectors.flagship_opportunity: Release the first OPEN Kazakh vision-language training corpus (QymyzCap, distilled captions + visual instructions) and prove it by training QymyzVLM-0.6B — the first sub-1B Kazakh VLM (SigLIP + QymyzLM, SmolVLM recipe). The entire sector currently hangs on ISSAI: their Qolda-4.3B is open-weights but its training data is closed, and Oylan's 10M-image/50M-QA corpus is fully closed — so no one else can train anything. An open corpus + a 7x-smaller model evaluated head-to-head against Qolda on ISSAI's own translated benchmarks (plus a native, commercially-licensed KazVLM-Bench) simultaneously breaks the data monopoly, gives the SLM paper its headline multimodal result, and makes the author's backbone the default starting point for Kazakh multimodal work.

en_zh_sota.name: spaCy trained pipelines (en_core_web_trf etc.)
en_zh_sota.numbers: ~25 languages with full trained pipelines (tagger+parser+NER+lemmatizer); en_core_web_trf ≈97.8% POS / ≈0.90 NER F1 (approx., per spaCy model release notes — exact page failed to load); MIT license; pip-installable, CPU-friendly sm variants
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The packaging bar: one `pip install` gives a production pipeline. Kazakh has zero presence in spaCy (not even a trained pipeline), so every kk engineer re-solves tokenize/POS/NER from scratch.

en_zh_sota.name: GECToR (Grammarly) — GEC as sequence tagging
en_zh_sota.numbers: F0.5 65.3/66.5 (CoNLL-2014), 72.4/73.6 (BEA-2019); ~10x faster inference than seq2seq; Apache-2.0
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The efficient-GEC architecture bar — a tagger small enough to serve cheaply, the exact regime a solo engineer with an RTX 2070 can replicate for Kazakh.

en_zh_sota.name: C4_200M synthetic GEC data recipe (Google)
en_zh_sota.numbers: 200M synthetic corrupted-clean sentence pairs generated from C4 via tagged corruption models; enabled near-SOTA GEC without new human annotation
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The method bar for building GEC in a language with no error-annotated corpus — the direct blueprint for a first Kazakh GEC dataset.

en_zh_sota.name: ChineseErrorCorrector3-4B
en_zh_sota.numbers: F0.5 0.4874 on NaCGEC (SOTA, Nov 2025), beating Huawei HW_TSC (0.4526); 4B params handling spelling + grammar jointly
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Shows the current ZH endpoint: one small-ish open model doing unified spell+grammar correction — exactly what a <=600M Kazakh SLM should aim to be a scaled-down version of.

en_zh_sota.name: MuCGEC / FCGEC (Chinese GEC benchmarks)
en_zh_sota.numbers: MuCGEC: multi-reference multi-source eval with char-level edit scoring; FCGEC: fine-grained error-typed corpus; both open
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The evaluation-infrastructure bar: ZH has multiple typed, multi-reference GEC benchmarks; Kazakh has zero GEC eval data of any kind.

en_zh_sota.name: LanguageTool
en_zh_sota.numbers: 31 supported languages, thousands of hand-written rules + neural components; open-core (LGPL); browser/Office integrations. Kazakh NOT among supported languages (verified against dev.languagetool.org/languages)
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The product bar for grammar checking: ubiquitous integrations. Its kk-shaped hole is both the gap evidence and a possible contribution channel (a kk module upstream).

en_zh_sota.name: Maverick (Sapienza NLP) — coreference
en_zh_sota.numbers: 83.6 avg CoNLL-F1 on OntoNotes with 500M params, outperforming 13B models; ACL 2024; models on HF
en_zh_sota.why_reference: Coref SOTA at exactly the parameter budget relevant here (0.5B); Kazakh has no coref dataset or model at all, and is absent from CorefUD/CRAC shared tasks.

en_zh_sota.name: Stanza (Stanford)
en_zh_sota.numbers: Neural UD pipelines (tokenize/POS/lemma/depparse/NER) for 70+ languages; Apache-2.0; its kk model exists but scores only ~87.9 UPOS / 57.4 LAS due to the tiny KTB treebank
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The multilingual academic-pipeline bar — and the proof that Kazakh's bottleneck is treebank size, not architecture.

en_zh_sota.name: N-LTP / HanLP (Chinese multi-task toolkits)
en_zh_sota.numbers: N-LTP: 6 tasks (CWS, POS, NER, DEP, SDP, SRL) in one multi-task model, SOTA/competitive on 5/6 (EMNLP 2021 demo); HanLP: multilingual with strong ZH, RESTful + native APIs
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The 'national-language toolkit' bar: ZH institutions shipped a single maintained platform covering all classic tasks — the closest Kazakh analog (TurkicNLP, Feb 2026) is 21 GitHub stars and weak parsing.

en_zh_sota.name: Hunspell ecosystem
en_zh_sota.numbers: De-facto spellcheck standard in LibreOffice/Firefox/Chrome/macOS; morphological affix compression handles some agglutination; GPL/LGPL/MPL
en_zh_sota.why_reference: The distribution bar for spelling: shipping a good .aff/.dic pair instantly reaches every office suite and browser — the highest-leverage delivery channel for a Kazakh speller.

kazakh_existing.name: Apertium-kaz (FST morphological analyzer + CG disambiguator)
kazakh_existing.status: USABLE, maintained — 36,595 stems, ~94.5% naive coverage on random corpora; GPL-3.0; actively consumed as the morphology backend of the new TurkicNLP toolkit (2026). The single strongest classic-NLP asset Kazakh has. Ongoing lexicon extension from the 15-volume Explanatory Dictionary.

kazakh_existing.name: UD Kazakh-KTB treebank
kazakh_existing.status: USABLE but frozen and tiny — 1,078 sentences / 10,536 words, CC BY-SA 4.0, in UD since v1.3 (2016), still the ONLY Kazakh UD treebank as of UD 2.18. No real train split ('train file is just a sample'; docs prescribe 10-fold CV). This is the hard ceiling on all kk parsing/tagging (LAS stuck at 57-60).

kazakh_existing.name: KazNERD (ISSAI NER dataset + models)
kazakh_existing.status: USABLE, high quality — 112,702 sentences, 136,333 annotations, 25 classes, CC BY 4.0; best model XLM-RoBERTa-large hits 97.22 F1. Caveat: single domain (TV news text) and the best checkpoint is a heavy 560M model.

kazakh_existing.name: KazSAnDRA (ISSAI sentiment) + RemBERT classifiers
kazakh_existing.status: USABLE — 180,064 reviews (4 domains, 1-5 stars), CC BY 4.0; best polarity F1 0.81, score-classification only 0.39 (large headroom). Naturally contains kk/ru code-switching and mixed scripts.

kazakh_existing.status: USABLE, brand-new, thin adoption (21 stars, 0 forks) — pip package wrapping Apertium FST + Stanza/Glot500 + KazNERD NER + 2021-standard transliteration for 24 Turkic languages; Apache-2.0. kazakh_existing.name: Kazakh GEC / grammar-checking resources
kazakh_existing.status: ABSENT — no error-annotated corpus, no synthetic GEC dataset, no corrector model, no benchmark; nearest neighbors are Turkish (GECTurk) and Russian (SAGE/RuSpellGold) resources. Only academic trace: a 2014 Springer paper on noisy-channel Kazakh spelling correction with no released artifact.

gaps.gap: No grammar correction (GEC) for Kazakh at any level: zero datasets, zero models, zero benchmark, zero LanguageTool support
gaps.why: EN has GECToR/LLM correctors and ZH has typed benchmarks + a SOTA 4B corrector; Kazakh has literally nothing. With the state pushing Latin-script transition (~2031, timeline fluid — original 2017 decree said 2025), millions of writers (students, civil servants, media) will produce error-heavy text in BOTH scripts with no tooling. This is simultaneously the biggest product opening in the sector.

gaps.gap: UD treebank is 1,078 sentences with no train split — the hard ceiling on parsing, tagging, and lemmatization
gaps.why: Every neural pipeline (Stanza, TurkicNLP/Glot500) tops out at ~88 UPOS / 57-60 LAS because that is all the gold syntax that exists. EN treebanks are 100x larger; even Kyrgyz gets treebank-translation papers. Nothing downstream (spaCy pipeline, coref, quality lemmatizer eval) can be properly trained or measured until this grows.

gaps.gap: Spell checking frozen at a ~53k-stem OpenOffice-era hunspell wordlist; no Latin-script (2021 alphabet) spelling support at all
gaps.why: A wordlist cannot cover an agglutinative language where one stem yields hundreds of valid surface forms — real-world coverage is poor and unmeasured. Meanwhile Apertium-kaz's 36.6k-stem FST with full affix morphology already encodes the solution; nobody has compiled it into distributable hunspell/browser artifacts. The Latin transition doubles the urgency: no speller exists for the new script.

gaps.gap: No spaCy pipeline (and no single maintained 'default toolkit') for Kazakh
gaps.why: The absence of `pip install kk_core_news_sm` is a tax on every downstream builder. TurkicNLP (Feb 2026) partially fills this but is new, thin (21 stars), GPL-encumbered on the FST path, and weak at parsing. The niche of 'the obvious default kk pipeline' is still open.

gaps.gap: Transliteration tools are naive char-maps: no named-entity awareness, no loanword handling, no public accuracy benchmark
gaps.why: Cyrillic->Latin conversion of real Kazakh text is NOT 1:1 — Russian loanwords, foreign proper names (Чайковский, Facebook), mixed kk/ru sentences, and ambiguous letters (и, у, ю, я) need context. Official qazlatyn.kz is a closed web tool; open alternatives are dumb rule tables. During a national script migration this is critical infrastructure with no quality floor established.

gaps.gap: No token-level kk/ru code-switch detector; code-switching supervision limited to 618 sentences + doc-level labels
gaps.why: Heavy kk/ru mixing is THE defining property of real Kazakhstani text. Without a detector you cannot cleanly filter SLM pretraining corpora (ru contamination inflates tokenizer fertility and wastes the 600M budget), build honest eval slices, or route text in products. kaznlp's langid is document-level and abandoned.

gaps.gap: No Kazakh coreference dataset or model; absent from all CorefUD/CRAC shared tasks
gaps.why: Real gap vs the EN bar (Maverick 83.6 F1) but low product urgency; matters mostly for the atlas's completeness map and long-horizon RAG/summarization quality. A small gold eval set would be a cheap first-of-kind paper artifact.

gaps.gap: Sentiment stuck at reviews-domain polarity (F1 0.81, best model is a huge RemBERT); score-level classification at 0.39; no aspect-based, no news/social eval
gaps.why: Something exists (KazSAnDRA), so this is refinement not absence — but the 0.39 score-classification number and the RemBERT-only serving story show how shallow the coverage is; the new 100k movie-review corpus makes a cross-domain upgrade cheap.

sectors.flagship_opportunity: The first Kazakh grammar-and-spell corrector, timed to the Latin-script transition. Nothing exists — no GEC dataset, no benchmark, no LanguageTool module, and the installed spell-check base is a ~53k-word 2010-era hunspell list that structurally cannot handle agglutination — while the state is migrating 13-16M speakers to a new alphabet (~2031), guaranteeing years of error-heavy writing in two scripts. The full stack is buildable solo: Apertium-kaz's FST (36.6k stems, 94.5% coverage) is a free corruption-and-validation oracle for a C4_200M-style synthetic corpus; kkwiki edit history yields a real-typo benchmark in a week; and the corrector itself is a <=600M fine-tune — meaning QymyzLM's killer demo, the standalone product (browser/Office speller + GEC API), and a first-of-kind paper artifact are all the same build. Whoever ships this owns the default writing tool for a national script migration.

sector_ranking.rationale: Zero kk-tagged embedding models or rerankers on HF (verified via HF API, Jul 2026), no benchmark, no human STS; the 'best Kazakh embedder' title is factually unclaimed — off-the-shelf mE5-large leads (MRR 0.909 KazQAD) and no fine-tune has beaten it. Feedstock (KazQAD, KazParC 372k, OPUS, 800k wiki passages) sits ready. This is the author's goal #2 with a ~1-month, <$100 path to owning both the measurement layer and the crown.

No morphology-aware analyzer in any mainstream search engine (only a 2018 ES 5.6 plugin), zero rerankers, KazQAD never contributed to MTEB, no RAG eval harness — while state demand is real (eGov AI agents scaling to 7M users by end-2026 on unadapted multilingual components). Overlaps heavily with embeddings; the two sectors are one campaign.

Zero open kk preference/DPO data (Sherkala's 3.5M pairs closed; the one kk DPO paper regularized around the absence), no safety classifier, no live arena, no contamination protocol on KazMMLU. Every open kk SLM is stuck at SFT-only — first publisher becomes the default dependency, including for QymyzLM's own DPO/RLVR paper stages.

GEC/grammar-checking is absolute zero (no dataset, model, benchmark, or LanguageTool module) heading into a national script migration; spelling is a 2010-era 53k wordlist that structurally can't handle agglutination. Apertium-kaz (36.6k stems, 94.5% coverage) is a free oracle nobody has operationalized. Parsing is capped by a 1,078-sentence treebank — an institution-shaped problem, unlike the rest.

Commercial engines and Tilmash exist, but nobody knows current SOTA — last systematic comparison used 2023-era models, and the likely-best open system (Hy-MT2, Apache-2.0, kk-tagged, May 2026) has zero published kk numbers. The measurement seat, the <600M on-device slot, en→kk generation, doc-level MT, and terminology control are all open lanes; the raw need is otherwise served by Google/Yandex.

The most active kk community sector: multiple credible 2026 fine-tunes (9.16-11.8% self-reported WER), Vosk, ISSAI, commercial APIs. Modeling is crowded, but numbers are mutually incomparable (different normalizations) — the open seat is the measurement layer (leaderboard + frozen normalization + hallucination/CS tracks), which is inference-only and instantly citation-anchoring.

Engines nominally cover kk via shared generic Cyrillic models (PaddleOCR's Cyrillic group trained on ~7.6k images total); no real-scan page-level benchmark exists (the country's entire real-image eval is 199 print images), no dedicated open kk model, and töte-jazu (Arabic-script kk) scores ~0 everywhere. Benchmark + rec-head are solo-scale; the KazNEB token unlock (82,853 books) is the strategic prize for SLM v2.

All ingredients open and unassembled: 271h CC-BY KazakhTTS2 + Apache-2.0 0.6B bases (Qwen3-TTS), four 2026 hobbyist finetunes with zero published metrics, no benchmark, RHVoice/Piper accessibility hole. A bench+finetune pair is a strong flagship — but it feeds neither the embedding crown nor the SLM paper's text claims, so it's campaign #2 material.

Technically the emptiest sector — no open X→kk speech output on Earth (SeamlessM4T-v2 excludes kk from its 35 output languages; Qwen3-Omni has kk in neither speech list), all domestic products closed with zero published numbers. But it's compute-heavy and depends on a chat-capable QymyzLM + streaming kk TTS existing first; wide open, wrong time for a solo builder.

ISSAI actively owns this: Qolda-4.3B open-weights, Oylan's 10M-image corpus closed, 8 translated eval suites published. The wedge (first OPEN kk VL training corpus + first sub-1B kk VLM) is real but quarter-scale in time and $500-1,100 in spend, competing against a funded institute. Cheap leaderboard/audit plays now; the model play is paper-v2 material.

cross_sector_synergies: One leaderboard codebase, five citation anchors: the HF-Space + frozen-protocol + results-dataset harness built for kk-MTEB is reused nearly verbatim for KazMT-Bench, KazASR-Bench, and later KazTTS-Bench and the VLM leaderboard — and these measured tables collectively ARE the data-driven backbone that differentiates the atlas from the existing narrative surveys.

MT engines are data pumps, not just models: the KazSynC back-translation pipeline and the round-trip paraphrase engine feed embedding contrastive pairs, QymyzLM SFT/MT training data, and code-switch eval generation from one codebase — Hy-MT2 verification (2 days) de-risks all three at once.

Apertium-kaz FST is the sector-spanning free oracle: BM25 stemmer/analyzer (retrieval), GEC corruption-and-validation engine (nlp-classics), case-agreeing number expansion for TTS text-norm and ASR ITN, hunspell 2.0 compilation, and inflected-form terminology matching for MT — one GPL asset, six deliverables.

The token-level kk-ru code-switch detector is one tool with five consumers: QymyzLM pretraining-corpus cleaning, embedding hard-negative mining, and the code-switch columns of the retrieval, MT, ASR, and safety benchmarks — which is why it ranks 4th despite being 'just' a classifier.

QymyzLM backbone multiplies: MT-tune, punctuation/casing restorer, RAG groundedness judge, code-switch query rewriter, GEC corrector, and later VLM (SigLIP+QymyzLM) and speech-in (whisper-encoder+projector) adapters — every downstream fine-tune is simultaneously a paper section and a shippable product, amortizing the pretraining cost.

KazLegal-Parallel (adilet.zan.kz, bilingual by law) serves four masters from one scrape: embedding hard positives, the only doc-level kk MT benchmark substrate, the legal RAG demo corpus, and terminology-compliance evaluation against Termincom's 21k state terms.

The two biggest untapped SLM token sources are cross-sector unlocks: ASR mass-transcription of yodas2-kk/podcasts yields 50-100M conversational tokens (the register missing from web crawls), and OCR of KazNEB's 82,853 books yields edited literary prose — both use the same quality-filter infrastructure with QymyzLM itself as the perplexity gate (the model curates its own future training data).

The flagship embedder cascades: it is the distillation source for the reranker, the future kk CLIP text tower via locked-image tuning, the retrieval leg of QazaqRAG, and the subject of the OCR-noise robustness study — one checkpoint, four surfaces, all refereed by kk-MTEB.

The qazlat Cyrillic↔Latin converter future-proofs four sectors at once (MT robustness, TTS Latin input, OCR Latin readiness, SLM corpus augmentation) ahead of the ~2031 transition, and the contamination-audit MinHash tooling doubles as the dedup layer for every dataset the campaign releases — benchmark hygiene and data hygiene are the same code.
